title: Count the Number of Good Partitions
statement:
The array `nums` holds positive integers. Cut it into one or more contiguous, non-empty pieces that keep the original order and together cover every element. Such a cutting is *good* when no number shows up in two different pieces, so every copy of a value lands in the same piece.

Return how many good cuttings exist, modulo `10^9 + 7`. Leaving the array whole counts as one cutting.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of cuts is exponential. Instead, ask which single cuts are allowed: a cut between positions `i - 1` and `i` is safe only if no value occurs on both sides. Sweeping left to right while tracking `reach`, the furthest last occurrence of any value seen so far, tells us exactly that: the cut is safe when `i > reach`. Safe cuts never interfere with one another, so each one is independently taken or skipped. With `m` safe cuts the answer is `2^m`.

## Approach

1. Record `lastIndex` for every value, the position of its final copy.
2. Start `answer = 1` and `reach = 0`.
3. For each `i`: if `i > reach`, everything before `i` is self-contained, so the cut before `i` is optional and `answer` doubles (mod `10^9 + 7`).
4. Extend `reach` to `lastIndex` of `nums[i]`, since the current piece must stretch at least that far.
5. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]`, so `lastIndex` maps each value to its own position.

- `i = 0`: `0 > 0` is false; `reach = 0`.
- `i = 1`: `1 > 0`, so `answer = 2`; `reach = 1`.
- `i = 2`: `2 > 1`, so `answer = 4`; `reach = 2`.
- `i = 3`: `3 > 2`, so `answer = 8`; `reach = 3`.

All three cuts are free, giving `8`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to fill the map and one pass to sweep.
- Space: O(n) for `lastIndex`.

## Pitfalls

- Take the modulus at every doubling; `2^m` overflows quickly (even in JavaScript, `2^99999` is far beyond exact integers).
- Do not double at `i = 0`: there is no cut before the first element.
- `reach` must be a running maximum; a later value with an earlier last copy must not shrink it, as in `[1, 2, 1, 3]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | `10^9 + 7` |
| `lastIndex` | value → index of its last occurrence |
| `answer` | number of good cuttings of the prefix seen so far |
| `reach` | furthest index the current piece is forced to include |
| `i` | current position in the sweep |

narration.3: Map each value to the index of its last copy.
narration.4: Walk the array once to fill the map.
narration.5: Later copies overwrite earlier ones, so the stored index is the last one.
narration.7: With no free cuts yet there is exactly one cutting: the whole array.
narration.8: reach is the furthest index the current piece is forced to cover.
narration.9: Sweep the positions from left to right.
narration.10: If i lies beyond reach, nothing before i reappears later, so cutting just before i is optional.
narration.11: An optional cut can be taken or skipped, doubling the count.
narration.13: The piece holding nums[i] must extend at least to that value's last copy.
narration.15: Every free cut doubled the count, so this is 2^m modulo 10^9 + 7.
